title: CompiledRule
description: One faithful compilation of a rule into an executable decision tree. A rule identifies a SET of defensible compilations; each instance of this schema is one sample from that set. Every node must be grounded in a quoted span of the source text.

compiler.description: Provenance of this compilation (model, prompt variant, date). Needed for k-sample divergence analysis.

range.description: For numeric fields: plausible [min, max], used by the fuzzer.

question.description: The question as it would be asked of the applicant/inspector.

supplier.description: Who produces this input (question #3 of the intake).

provenance_class.description: Burden ladder: a=known offhand/self-attestation; b=document already in household records; c=must be requested from an institution; d=artifact applicant must create; e=artifact a paid professional must create; f=requires a government act (inspection, appointment). Costs per class live in burden_priors.json; per-field overrides go in burden_override.

operationalizations.description: Schema v3 (input-level discretion, per Dan Ho's 'age can be defined 5 ways'): the defensible ways this fact can be operationalized, and who fixes it. More than one entry = lurking discretion inside an 'objective' input.

fixed_by.description: Who resolves which definition governs (clerk, statute, regulation, custom).

acquisition.description: The real-world act that yields this input (e.g. 'application_form', 'site_inspection', 'records_request', 'professional_report'). Fields sharing an acquisition event share its cost: one inspection observes many facts.

burden_override.description: Optional field-specific costs overriding the class prior.

sensitive.description: True if supplying this input exposes the applicant to legal/financial risk (e.g. admitting an unpermitted structure exists). Psychological-cost axis.

evidence.description: What document/observation would establish this input.

quote.description: Verbatim quote from the source text this node implements.

score.description: Score-aggregation decision (schema v3): a weighted sum of condition items compared against thresholds — required for point systems (health-inspection score sheets, grade cutoffs) that boolean branching cannot represent. A node carries EITHER predicate OR score OR outcome.

expr.description: Required iff type=objective: JsonLogic condition; when true, `points` are added.

thresholds.description: Score bands mapping to targets (node ids). A band is [min, max]; omit max for open-ended.

atoms.description: Schema v3: sub-conditions of a multi-part decision, each span-pinned — the decision/condition split (a decision may aggregate several testable atoms; crosswalks align at the decision level, atoms stay pinned to text).

type.description: objective = a clerk could decide it from the listed inputs with no discretion (expr REQUIRED); judgment = requires a discretionary assessment by the decider (no expr; the executor treats it as indeterminate and explores both branches); reference = delegates to another provision not compiled here (target REQUIRED).

expr.description: JsonLogic-style expression over input field names. Required iff type=objective. Supported ops: var, ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, and, or, !, in, +, -, *, /, if, missing.

target.description: For type=reference: citation of the delegated provision.

monotonicity.description: Metamorphic invariants: for each input field, '+' means increasing the field can only move this predicate toward true, '-' the reverse, '0' irrelevant. These are testable claims about the STATUTE, declared at compile time and checked against every compilation by the case simulator.

conditions.description: For conditional_approve: what must be corrected.

flags.description: Deep-research triggers. REF = unresolved cross-reference; LOCAL = meaning is fixed by the implementing jurisdiction; EMPIRICAL = needs real-world data; TACIT = below the articulation floor, needs human expert elicitation.

non_operative.description: Coverage contract: every subdivision of the source that produced no node, with the reason (definition, fee provision, notice requirement...). Nothing may be silently dropped.
